resources.string: VitalySpeak shows a floating microphone button while you type. Tap it to dictate; your speech is transcribed and the text is inserted into the field you are typing in. VitalySpeak uses this service only to show the button, to detect when a text field is in use, to insert your dictated text, and (optionally) to use the volume-down button as a command key while recording. It does not read, collect or share the content of your screen.

Used when the speech is unclear

The speech recogniser knows about 100 languages. Left to guess, it sometimes picks the wrong one: a strong accent or a short phrase can come out as a different language, or translated.

• With one language selected, recognition is told exactly what to expect. That is the most accurate and the fastest option.
• With several, VitalySpeak checks which language was recognised. If it isn't one of yours, that part is transcribed again in your primary language.
• Your languages are also passed to the AI cleanup, so it keeps every language exactly as you spoke it, even when you switch mid-sentence, and never translates.

So add only the languages you really use.

Why VitalySpeak uses the Accessibility service
VitalySpeak does not read, store or send the content of your screen or of other apps. It does not log your keystrokes, does not perform actions on your behalf, and has no ads or analytics.

The microphone is used only after you tap the button. The recording is sent to Groq, Inc. with your own API key, to be transcribed and (if AI cleanup is on) cleaned up, and the text comes back to your phone. Nothing goes to the developer. Recordings are deleted from your phone after transcription unless you choose to keep them; your text history stays on your phone until you delete it.
